editorial:
Imagine a world where a rich, bored housewife decides that her new hobby is saving the world through a quirky new religion. You get to follow Susan, a socialite who has plenty of money but not much focus. She basically ignores her husband and kids because she is too busy trying to lead a spiritual movement. It feels like a lighthearted look at how people with too much free time can get carried away with strange ideas. The movie has a breezy, funny vibe that makes the family drama feel more like a comedy of errors than a heavy tragedy.

You will really love the acting here, as the lead actress makes Susan feel like someone you might actually know in real life. The pacing is steady, though some parts might feel a bit slow if you are used to modern action movies. It is a great pick if you enjoy old-school stories about family clashes and social status. To get the best experience, you should try renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection so you can see all the beautiful old sets in high detail.
endingExplained: In the end, Susan finally realizes that her obsession with the religious group has pushed her family away. She has a wake-up call and understands that being a good mother and wife is more important than leading a cult. She drops her grand plans for the movement and focuses on fixing her home life. Everything wraps up happily as she chooses her loved ones over her fame, leaving the viewers with a sweet lesson about priorities.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old Hollywood comedies and family stories.
